item.title: Jamie Carragher warns Ryan Gravenberch may never recover after Andoni Iraola picks teenager Trey Nyoni against Arsenal
item.description: Liverpool v Manchester City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jamie Carragher fears Ryan Gravenberch may never recover from being dropped for 19-year-old Trey Nyoni, who makes his first Premier League start against Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday. Andoni Iraola has left the Netherlands international on the bench for the crunch clash, a decision Carragher believes will be "a mighty blow" for the experienced midfielder. Nyoni handed first Premier League start against Arsenal Iraola has made a bold call by handing Nyoni his first Premier League start in Sunday's huge clash, with Gravenberch left among the substitutes. The teenager has already made 20 appearances for Liverpool, 14 of them this season, and has started in the Champions League. Gravenberch had returned for the win over Brighton after a one-game ban for his red card against Manchester City, and started alongside Nyoni in Wednesday's Carabao Cup win over Chelsea on penalties after a 1-1 draw. Alexis Mac Allister partners the youngster behind Florian Wirtz, while Dominik Szoboszlai is on the bench after injury. Carragher: It's always difficult for the senior player to recover Speaking on Sky Sports, Carragher said: "The one thing that has stood out with the manager so far is he's not afraid to make big decisions. He dropped Gravenberch really early, after the first game of the season, away at Newcastle. He's left [Milos] Kerkez out, a player who he knows before as well. He's changed the wingers in and out at different times. "What I would say is, I think we all go back to being a young player; the first time as a youngster when you're ever picked ahead of what you [think] is an established player. It's always difficult, I think, for the senior player to ever recover from that. Not that he can't come back, but Iraola's saying he's got more trust in a 19-year-old kid who's only getting better and his career is going one way. I think that will be a mighty blow for Gravenberch." Recalling his own breakthrough, he added: "I always remember it was Michael Thomas, central midfield, the manager Roy Evans putting me in." Iraola trusts Nyoni '100 per cent' as Sturridge backs the call Explaining his selection to Sky Sports, Iraola said: "It's not about me, it's about Trey. He has shown that he has the level. He covers a lot of space and he's aggressive without the ball, he's calm in possession and he's good in communicating with his team-mates." item.title: Fox put together rare performance in Spurs' victory over Timberwolves
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) drives against Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jonathan Kuminga (24) at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves 121-111. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs All-Star guard De'Aaron Fox accomplished something in Saturday's 121-111 victory over Minnesota that has rarely happened in franchise history. Fox finished with 22 points on 8-of-10 shooting from the field, a team-high eight rebounds (including two on the offensive end) and a team-best seven assists in 35 minutes, marking just the fifth game in which a Spur has had 20-plus points, eight-plus rebounds and seven-plus assists while shooting 80% from the floor. Jakob Poeltl (2022), Gene Banks (1983, 1985) and Billy Paultz (1978) are the other players to do it. "Just trying to be efficient, trying to affect the game in different ways, get downhill," said Fox, who notched his first 20-point game of the season in helping the Spurs win their fourth in a row to improve to 4-2. Through six games, Fox is averaging 16.5 points on 57.6% shooting, 4.8 rebounds, a team-high 7.0 assists and 1.5 steals. "We know to go to him," said All-Star center Victor Wembanyama, who led the Spurs with 43 points. "We know to put the ball in his hands. He knows to go get the ball. And he's been reacting defensively too. So, it's a true point guard." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: In a city under attack, Canelo Alvarez became the definition of calm under fire
item.description: The reason why Mexican boxers tend to be so revered has a lot to do with their willingness to put themselves in harm’s way. Consult the archives and you will discover they all did it: Chavez, Sanchez, Lopez, Marquez, Olivares, Saldivar, Zarate, Barrera, Morales and so on. Not only did each of these men put themselves in harm’s way, they did so with a rare grace and intelligence, almost as if it was part of the strategy; something they had, in the 14-foot-by-14-foot rings in Mexico, over time learned to master. To any great Mexican fighter, the idea of being in harm’s way means opportunity. More than just an act of bravado, it increases the likelihood of an opponent opening up, getting careless, and offering a target to hit. It also means action, excitement, admiration. If in doubt, just listen to the crowd on fight night. Seemingly, the more these men put themselves in harm’s way, the louder the arena becomes and the more people are inclined to watch. Sometimes, with such a price placed on machismo , putting themselves in harm’s way can feel like the only way for these warriors. With all that said, few Mexican boxers have ever put themselves in harm’s way quite like Saul “Canelo” Alvarez did this weekend in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia . If it wasn’t enough to face and defuse the attacks of Christian Mbilli, the WBC super middleweight champion, the fighter from Guadalajara had to also contend with the pervasive threat of attacks from Iranian-supported Houthi rebels , which have so far claimed the lives of at least 20 people and injured at least 370 in Riyadh. As well it might, this put a very different spin on the idea of a Mexican boxer finding themselves in harm’s way. No matter the talent or courage, to come through the ordeal and return home in one piece would require more than just an ability to fight inside, a granite chin, and short punches. It would also require nerve, perhaps even an ignorance. Most of all, it would require an element of good fortune on the part of Alvarez and all who traveled. For Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez, the show must go on. Mark Robinson via Getty Images Indeed, just 48 hours before the first bell, everybody in Riyadh had been warned via an emergency alert sent to mobile phones to be vigilant and prepared. According to those on the ground, the message received was as follows: “Warning. City of Riyadh is under a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm, stay indoors or in a safe place away from windows and doors, and follow the instructions of Civil Defense.” This was then accompanied by a social media post from Turki Alalshikh, the man responsible for bringing Mbilli vs. Alvarez to Riyadh, which said, quite simply: “May God protect Riyadh and all who are in it.” Of course, the biggest challenge for Alvarez and Mbilli would have been maintaining focus and concentration, both throughout fight week and on the night itself. item.title: Alcaraz wins Vienna Open to maintain perfect record
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz is a seven-time Grand Slam winner [Getty Images] Carlos Alcaraz powered to a straight-set win over Alex de Minaur to win the Vienna Open and maintain his perfect record in ATP 500 events this year. The Spanish second seed triumphed 6-1 6-4 in 87 minutes for his 16th straight win at that level in 2026. Alcaraz has won 26 straight matches at ATP 500 events - a run that goes back to the 2025 Barcelona Open, where he lost to Holger Rune. The 23-year-old's run this year includes titles in Doha and Tokyo. "I tried to be aggressive and show him that if he wants to win, he has to play better, more aggressive, more solid, and be smarter than me," said Alcaraz. "I'm just really happy that at the end I found my way, played great, and obviously it has been a really emotional and amazing week for me." Alcaraz started the match strongly, with his groundstrokes causing De Minaur problems. De Minaur took five of the seven games in the first set to deuce, but it was Alcaraz's quality at key moments that made the difference as he secured three breaks of serve. Alcaraz continued to apply pressure in the second set, and while De Minaur's trademark defence helped the 27-year-old Australian save three break points, he could not fend off championship point. After a gripping rally, Alcaraz whipped a forehand winner across court to seal victory, before raising both arms in celebration. The win was Alcaraz's seventh against De Minaur, maintaining his perfect head-to-head record. item.title: How Dart revived career with help of Wimbledon champion
item.description: In the hour following her first WTA title win, Britain's Harriet Dart had little time to respond to the stream of congratulatory messages flashing up on her phone. Most pressing was making a call to her proud parents, Nick and Susie, who had been watching the final with friends at their local tennis club in north London, and her sister Phoebe. The next person she spoke to was 2013 Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli. Dart has been coached by the French former world number seven since the start of the season on a part-time basis, and she credits Bartoli for helping her achieve what some thought was beyond her. On Sunday, with Bartoli watching from home, the world number 115 won the Guangzhou Open in China by beating rising Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger. "It's been quite incredible to work with Marion, and I was really fortunate she was open to working with me," Dart, 30, told BBC Sport in a video call from Guangzhou. "I'm obviously at a very different stage of my career to someone who is, say, 20. But I still feel I have a lot to improve and there are gains to be made. "She really believes in me - that means the world to me. Seeing a Grand Slam champion having that belief has made me believe a lot more in myself." Britain's Dart wins first WTA title in 'wild week' When Dart started working with Bartoli, she was ranked outside the top 160. The pair live close to each other in Dubai and spend training blocks together there when Dart is not on the road. Dart and Bartoli, who has a young family, are not travelling full-time together on tour, but there have been opportunities for them to work on the ground, particularly during this year's Grand Slam tournaments. Dart says 42-year-old Bartoli still hitting the ball "really well" in practice is another benefit of the partnership. In Guangzhou, Dart was accompanied by her fitness trainer Dario Gonfiantini and boyfriend Stephen Falck. Without her coach, Dart had to largely rely on figuring things out herself - with the help of Bartoli sending over observational notes. Dart is projected to rise to 83rd on Monday after lifting the Guangzhou trophy to cap a stunning second half of the season. Dart has won 19 of her 24 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon, taking her overall record on the WTA Tour this season to 23 victories from 34 matches - the highest winning percentage of her career. "More than anything, Marion is just a great person. She cares about me as a person first and foremost, as well as improving me as a tennis player, of course," Dart said. "It's been invaluable and amazing for her to share her experiences to make me better. "I've learned a lot from her and look forward to continuing to learn more. I hope we will be able to spend more weeks together next year." item.title: Chinese state TV fails to air Real Madrid match after Mbappe row
item.description: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe scored in Sunday's La Liga clash against Racing Santander, but viewers in China were unable to see the goal after state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast the match (ANDER GILLENEA) Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast a Real Madrid La Liga match on Sunday after star forward Kylian Mbappe caused a furore in China with remarks he made about former leader Mao Zedong. The match between Real Madrid and Racing Santander began at 1515 GMT but was not broadcast on either of CCTV's two sports channels, AFP reporters saw. None of the other matches from the 11th round of La Liga have been broadcast live on public television so far. A viral video in recent days showed Mbappe referring to Mao as a "dictator", prompting the body overseeing CCTV to say it would halt broadcasts of the top Spanish league. Mbappe, Real and La Liga later all said sorry for his remarks, and China's foreign ministry said it took the player's apology "seriously". Asked by AFP before the weekend, La Liga said that Chinese television had previously shown all games live, without specifying which platforms hosted the broadcasts. AFP journalists did find live broadcasts of matches on Migu, a digital streaming service owned by the state-owned China Mobile telecom network. That included Barcelona's 6-1 win over Alaves on Saturday. However, the Racing Santander–Real Madrid match did not appear to be broadcast on Sunday on Migu. China Media Group (CMG), which oversees CCTV, had said it had moved on Monday to suspend La Liga broadcasts, adding that apologies from La Liga, Mbappe and Real Madrid were "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the furore. The viral video showed Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme about him he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator". This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. Mbappe later apologised for his "ill-judged" comments, La Liga said it "deeply" regretted them, and Real followed suit. CCTV's sports website later reported that CMG had acknowledged the apologies, but it remains unclear whether talks to defuse the situation have begun. China is a huge market for European football, with CCTV also carrying matches from the Premier League as well as the German, French and Italian top flights. Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said on Saturday that the club had "done our part" to put the controversy behind them. It is taboo in China to crack jokes about Mao, who died in 1976 and whose drastic policies are blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths. Major Chinese brands cancelled sponsorship deals with Mbappe after his comments. Various overseas sports leagues and players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China. item.description: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: Running back Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets is checked for injury during the second half of an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Breece Hall will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Las Vegas Raiders today. Hall will be inactive for the fifth consecutive week after he suffered a quadriceps injury against the Detroit Lions in the Jets’ third game of the 2026 season. The Jets are hopeful Hall will finally get back into the lineup next week against the Kansas City Chiefs. Hall’s absence has created an opportunity for Braelon Allen at running back, and Allen has taken full advantage. In the four games Allen has started in Hall’s absence this season Allen has put together two 100+ rushing yards games. Overall, Allen has averaged 4.6 yards per carry this season while already posting career highs in rushing yards with 418 and yards from scrimmage with 493. Allen has arguably been a more effective back than Hall, and he has presumably earned a larger role in the Jets’ offense even when Hall is back in the lineup. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Breece Hall David Bailey Joseph Ossai Nahshon Wright Tim Patrick Kohl Levao Max Mitchell Notable among those names is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. Unfortunately that signing has not worked out for Wright or the Jets. Indianapolis traded two of their best franchise players: guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner . item.description: Como 1907 v Venezia FC - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Cesc Fabregas has admitted that Como were fortunate to walk away with three points after a controversial VAR decision went in their favour during a narrow 1-0 victory over Venezia. A first-half penalty from Lucas Da Cunha proved to be the difference at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, lifting the Lariani to 23 points in the Serie A standings. Fabregas admits to fortune in narrow victory The narrow triumph keeps Como in the hunt for European spots, leaving them just two points adrift of second-placed Inter and five points behind league leaders Lazio . However, the result was not without its share of drama, as a potential penalty for Venezia involving Luis Milla was overturned by the match officials. 'When I saw it, it looked like a clear penalty to me. Before coming here, I asked whether it was a penalty or not. It’s not me saying it, but I was told it wasn’t, because Luis doesn’t move his arm and is trying to keep it out of the way,' the manager told TuttoMercatoWeb . 'It looked like a penalty to me, we were lucky, but people who understand it better than me, professionals, said it wasn’t. Ours? That was clearer. If the ball reaches Tasos and he isn’t touched from behind, it’s a goal. It’s difficult, and I’m saying that honestly.' Handling a congested fixture schedule Como are currently navigating a demanding period of the season, with a Champions League trip to face Lens on Wednesday - where they currently sit ninth in the table with six points from three matches - before a massive domestic clash against Inter next Sunday. Fabregas admitted that the relentless pace of modern football is taking a toll on his squad, particularly given that the group is not accustomed to such a high volume of matches. 'Nothing on the pitch is easy, and today we saw there’s incredible value in this victory. We’ve played a lot of games away from home. I give a lot of value to what we did, and it isn’t trivial. It’s very difficult to win in football, I see it every week, and today was a fundamental game. Venezia had one shot on target. We didn’t concede anything, and the lads aren’t used to this kind of schedule, one game after another. We’re practically not training, but we have to continue with this mentality,' Fabregas explained during his post-match assessment. Managing injuries and tactical solutions The manager’s job has been made more difficult by a growing injury list, particularly in wide areas where Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez are both currently sidelined. This was a game that in a normal year, we would’ve seen as an opportunity to get a bonus win in what otherwise would’ve been a hard road conference game. This was never supposed to be a game we had a serious chance in, but given everything else that’s happened this season, that truth rings ever more clear. There’s a lot of reasons why this 2026 Georgia Tech team should have been good. The running back room was nationally touted. Alberto Mendoza carried a popular football family name and some experience. Our new defensive coordinator had a good track record of creating turnovers. The incoming players weren’t all-timers, but certainly projected to be better than last year’s pourous defense. Doesn’t matter now. Last night was the nail in the coffin for this season if we weren’t already shut in the casket. Tech can only get to 6-6 this season, but it would require beating two projected College Football Playoff teams in Wake Forest and Athens Community College. Head coach Brent Key has had some luck in the past, but not that level of luck. At this point, if there’s anything redeeming about this season, you’d have to make it up out of thin air. item.title: Arizona football opens as one-score favorite vs. TCU
item.description: LUBBOCK, TEXAS - OCTOBER 31: Giovanni Richardson #5 of the Arizona Wildcats runs the ball during the second half of the game against the Texas Tech Red Raiders at Galaxy Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Lubbock, Texas. (Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images Arizona football is on a short week with the TCU Horned Frogs coming to town for a Friday night matchup. Arizona (6-2) and TCU (4-4) will kickoff with a late 8:15 p.m. MST start at Casino Del Sol Stadium on Friday. The game will be televised on ESPN. Arizona enters the game as a 7.5-point favorite, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is 44.5 points. The Wildcats are coming off of a 34-26 defeat to Texas Tech, a result that could cost Arizona in its chances of competing for a spot in the Big 12 Championship game. Arizona is currently in a four-way tie for third place in the conference standings (3-2), and the two teams immediately ahead in the standings own a head-to-head win over the Wildcats. Arizona is 3-5 this season against the spread (ATS) after failing to cover the 4.5-point line against Texas Tech. Brent Brennan ’s group had covered three straight games before Saturday. Arizona is 2-2 ATS at home. TCU is also 3-5 ATS and is coming off a cover in its 22-16 home win over Kansas on Saturday. TCU was favored by 5.5 points. The Horned Frogs, coached by Sonny Dykes , got off to an 0-2 start in conference play with losses to UCF and BYU. TCU responded with a win at Baylor followed by a home loss to West Virginia. TCU has the second-lowest scoring offense in the Big 12, averaging 23.3 points per game compared to Arizona’s 34.9. TCU’s 22 points it scored against Kansas were its most in a conference game. TCU’s offense is led by its passing game, which averages 276 yards, fourth-most in the Big 12 behind Oklahoma State, Arizona and Baylor. Senior quarterback Jaden Craig, a Harvard transfer, ranks 11th nationally with 2,207 passing yards. He has 11 touchdown passes to six interceptions. Defense is another story, though, as TCU has the top scoring defense in the conference with 14.1 points per game allowed. Arizona’s defense gives up 18.9 points. TCU has held all eight opponents it’s faced to 21 points or fewer. Arizona by contrast has scored 21 or more points in seven of eight games.

item.title: Man Utd making it harder for Juventus to sign Premier League star
item.description: Man Utd making it harder for Juventus to sign Premier League star Juventus are interested in signing Rayan Aït-Nouri from Manchester City as the defender struggles for regular game time since joining the Premier League club. The Bianconeri are looking to strengthen their left-back position and see him as a potential option. Juventus have been searching for new players in that role for some time. They already have several options in the squad, but they believe that Aït-Nouri could be tempted to join them, either in January or at the end of the season. Juventus eye a move Because he rarely plays at City, Aït-Nouri could be open to a move in January. Juventus would be keen to complete a deal , as they look to add quality to their defensive options and improve the competition for places in the left-back position. However, Juventus are not the only club monitoring the situation. According to Tuttojuve , Manchester United are the latest team to show interest in Aït-Nouri, adding competition for his signature. The Red Devils see him as one of the best options to replace Luke Shaw and would make efforts to sign him if City are willing to sell. That interest could make it more difficult for Juventus to secure the defender, especially if other clubs also enter the race. (Photo by Dan Mullan/Getty Images) A choice for Ait-Nouri A move to Manchester United could be straightforward for Aït-Nouri, as he would not need to change cities or learn a new language. Staying in the Premier League would also allow him to continue playing in a league he already knows well. However, he may prefer a fresh challenge away from English football. Juventus could offer him the opportunity to play in Serie A and compete for a club with a strong history, although they would need to convince him that they can provide regular playing time. Juventus remain interested in Aït-Nouri, but they face competition from Manchester United and potentially other top clubs. The defender’s lack of game time at Manchester City could work in Juventus’ favour, but they will need to act quickly if they want to secure his signature.

item.title: Keys before kickoff: Cowboys vs Cardinals Week 8
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images The 3-4 Dallas Cowboys look to begin a winning streak this week, facing off against the 2-5 Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. Here are three keys to the game. Run. The. Ball. Again. This is a copy and paste headline from last week’s keys before kickoff against the Eagles. Realistically, the mental reminder to run the ball should be the priority just about every week. This football team is simply better, as any team would be, with a dominant rushing attack. Dak Prescott thrives off the play-action, the receivers face lighter coverages when teams have to commit resources in the box, and the defense gets to rest while the offense works down the field on an eight-minute drive. Against Philadelphia last week, Brian Schottenheimer remembered his team features one of the NFL’s best run blocking offensive lines. Dallas ran the ball on 37 designed attempts, paying immediate dividends in a 38-21 win over their division rival. This week against the Cardinals, the plan should be similar. This Cardinals defense has struggled against the run throughout the season, ranking 29th in rush success rate allowed, per SumerSports. It’s an extremely malleable defense that changes the looks they give opposing offenses weekly, but even with those changes they have not been able to slow down the rushing attack much this season. And when they commit the resources in the box to slow down Williams, Dallas should be able to exploit the secondary with their big playmakers on the outside. Contain Trey McBride The Cardinals tight end leads the NFL in receptions (59 for 472 yards with four touchdowns) and is Arizona’s clear number one threat. He’s a volume target for quarterback Jacoby Brissett on an offense that lacks much firepower elsewhere. Dallas will need to contain McBride in the slot, out wide, on screens, on downfield throws, and eliminate the big yards after the catch. McBride truly is the ultimate weapon that deserves the utmost respect from opposing defenses each week. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker will have to devise a game plan to limit the one big weapon Arizona possesses. If he’s able to do so, this is a game that Dallas should win relatively easily, regardless of the history between the two teams. Get off to a quick start The quality of the Cowboys opponents have helped the defense play better over the last three weeks, at least from the perspective of the final scoreboard. But they are still far from being considered a “good” defense. One of those reasons is the fact that they cannot seem to get consistent stops early. Last week against a bad Eagles offense, Dallas surrendered two touchdowns on the first two drives. They would go on to let up just seven points for the rest of the game, but the lack of early success will certainly bite them if it continues this season. Andreas Almgren beat Yemaneberhan Crippa and Kamohelo Mofolo to gold (Reuters) The 31-year-old did not disappoint, timing his surge perfectly to win by 13 seconds in a time of 2:06:01 – continuing an excellent year that also saw him win continental gold over 10,000m on the track in Birmingham. In the women’s race through the five boroughs, Sheila Chepkirui claimed her second New York City marathon success. Sheila Chepkirui won back her New York City marathon title (Reuters) The Kenyan had previously won the title in 2024 and escaped from compatriot Hellen Obiri in the final miles, with home hope Jessica McClain finishing quickly to snatch second. item.title: Cowboys trade rumors: Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat mentioned again
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - OCTOBER 04: Josh Sweat #10 of the Arizona Cardinals during the game against the New York Giants on October 3, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It is starting to feel inevitable. There is still a week and change to go until the 2026 NFL trade deadline, but it at the very least feels more likely than not that the Dallas Cowboys are going to figure something out to land Arizona Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat. Adam Schefter stirred the pot of it all once again on Sunday morning. There is interest in Cardinals OLB Josh Sweat, per sources. A team to watch with Sweat is the Cowboys, who will get an up close look at him today, when Dallas hosts Arizona. pic.twitter.com/mNa42KxN1z — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 1, 2026 We are going on a couple of weeks with Sweat continually being connected to the Cowboys. First word popped up in a serious way on October 21st by way of ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler . Recent days have seen other ESPN figures mention it as a possibility as well and obviously Schefter did so once again on Sunday. This is why this feels rather inevitable. There is a lot of smoke building around the idea of Sweat, who plays against the Cowboys on Sunday with his current team in the Arizona Cardinals, getting moved to Dallas. It remains to be seen how the Cowboys could even pull something like this off. At the moment they have only four draft picks for 2027 (1, 2, 4, and 7) and have already dipped into their 2028 capital by executing a trade for Joey Porter Jr. a few weeks back.
